outcome: No settlement of the number-field conjecture in general since 26 January 2024: the in-window number-field results are partial (split smooth quintic del Pezzo surfaces over number fields, a chordal cubic fourfold over Q in thin-set form, subvarieties of toric varieties over Q with the constant not identified), one in-window counterexample to the closed-set (Zariski-open) form for specific singular del Pezzo surfaces (Gao, June 2024), and several function-field, geometric-Manin and log analogues; no AI system is credited with a counting result for this bullet.
problem_asks: (1) For a Fano variety X over a field the bullet does not name (the standard reading is a number field K) and an anticanonical height H: the number N(B) of K-rational points of H-height at most B grows like c times B times (log B) to the power rho(X) minus 1, with rho(X) the Picard rank; both the power of B (1, for anticanonical height) and the exponent of log are asserted. (2) The points counted lie in 'certain subsets' of X(K): the bullet asserts that the asymptotic holds on some subset obtained by removing an exceptional set, without saying which set or what kind. Manin's original reading removes a proper Zariski-closed set; the modern reading removes a thin set (Peyre). The bullet does not choose. (3) The claim is universal over Fano varieties: every Fano variety (no class is named) admits such a subset with the asymptotic. (4) The leading constant c is not stated in the bullet text; the standard conjecture (Peyre) takes c to be Peyre's constant. This is included because the standard statement includes it; it is not in the frozen wording. (5) 'Distribution' is read as the asymptotic count by height. Equidistribution is not named in the wording; some versions include it, so this is a reading choice.

events.what_happened: Runxuan Gao, 'A Zariski dense exceptional set in Manin's conjecture: dimension 2' (arXiv 2207.04348, v1 9 Jul 2022; v2 12 Aug 2022; v3 18 May 2023; comment 'final version to appear in Research in Number Theory'). The abstract (opened) and full text (opened) construct a del Pezzo surface of degree 1 whose geometric exceptional set, in the sense of the conjectural construction of Lehmann, Sengupta and Tanimoto, is Zariski dense: the first counterexample to the original (closed-set) form of Manin's conjecture in dimension 2, in characteristic 0. Assuming finiteness of Tate–Shafarevich groups of elliptic curves over Q with j-invariant 0, there are infinitely many such counterexamples.
events.delivers: A counterexample to the closed-set form of Manin's conjecture on the degree-1 del Pezzo surface S: w^2 = z^3 + m^2(x^6 + y^6) in P(1,1,2,3) over a number field k containing Q(sqrt(-3)), under hypotheses (positive Mordell–Weil rank of an elliptic curve E in the family, Picard rank 1 for S). Dimension 2 only. The thin-set form is not addressed in what I read.
events.remains: The thin-set (Peyre) form for these surfaces; all other del Pezzo surfaces; the infinitude statement is conditional on a Tate–Shafarevich finiteness assumption.
events.doubts: The fetched text is inconsistent on the Picard rank and degree in one example (it writes 'rank 11' and 'degree 11' where the equation indicates 1, which the fetch tool attributed to rendering). Check the PDF before relying on the example.
events.direction: Cuts against the closed-set form of Manin's conjecture in dimension 2 for this surface; the thin-set form is not contradicted by anything I read.
events.object: A degree-1 del Pezzo surface S given by the equation w^2 = z^3 + m^2(x^6 + y^6) in weighted projective space P(1,1,2,3) over a number field k containing Q(sqrt(-3)); the elliptic curve E in the family parametrises rational curves in |-2K_S|, and a section of the family meets all but finitely many fibres at smooth points, which gives Zariski density of the geometric exceptional set. Explicit: the surface is written down and an example m = 7 is given. Infinitely many m come from Dirichlet's theorem, conditional on Sha finiteness.

events.what_happened: Pieropan and Schindler, 'Points of bounded height on certain subvarieties of toric varieties' (arXiv 2403.19397, v1 28 Mar 2024; v2 7 Oct 2024, minor revision; Algebra & Number Theory 19 (2025), 2281–2306, DOI 10.2140/ant.2025.19.2281). events.what_happened: Runxuan Gao, 'Quasi-étale covers of Du Val del Pezzo surfaces and Zariski dense exceptional sets in Manin's conjecture' (arXiv 2406.16240, v1 23 Jun 2024; v2 17 Aug 2024; v3 4 Mar 2025, comment 'major revision, Sections 3.3, 4.3 and 4.4 are new'; 37 pages; no journal reference on the page). The abstract (opened) says the paper classifies quasi-étale covers of Du Val del Pezzo surfaces (extending Miyanishi–Zhang), constructs singular del Pezzo surfaces with Zariski dense exceptional sets in degrees 1, 2 and 3, and shows there are none in degree at least 4. The full text (first 100,000 of about 145,000 characters) gives Theorem 1.2: a degree-3 surface of type 4A1 and a degree-2 surface of type D4+3A1 where Manin's conjecture fails for some height for any proper closed exceptional set; a degree-2 surface of type 3A2 and a degree-1 surface of type E6+A2 where every dense open subset has the lower bound B(log B)^(rho−1), so the exceptional sets are Zariski dense. The abstract says the closed-set form fails for these examples.

events.delivers: Counterexamples to the closed-set (Zariski-open) form of Manin's conjecture for four specific singular Du Val del Pezzo surfaces of degrees 1, 2 and 3 (types 4A1, D4+3A1, 3A2, E6+A2), and none in degree 4 or higher. Over characteristic 0 (the classification is over C). The thin-set form for these surfaces is not established in the text I read.

events.directly_checkable: The surfaces are given by explicit equations in Theorem 1.2 (Du Val types listed above), so their defining data can be checked by hand; the Zariski density of the exceptional sets rests on the paper's argument, which I did not verify.
events.doubts: Single-author preprint with no journal reference. The v3 'major revision' added Sections 3.3, 4.3 and 4.4 that I did not compare with v1 or v2. Only the first 100,000 characters of the full text were read, so the Zariski-density argument was not checked in detail. No independent check was found. The ICMS talk abstract (not opened) claims the paper determines the LST conjectural exceptional set for these examples; the text I read does not confirm this.
events.direction: Cuts against the closed-set (Zariski-open) form of Manin's conjecture for these specific surfaces. As far as the text I read goes, not contradicted for the thin-set form.
events.object: Four singular Du Val del Pezzo surfaces with explicit equations in Theorem 1.2: degree 3, type 4A1; degree 2, type D4+3A1 (Manin fails for some height for any proper closed exceptional set); degree 2, type 3A2; degree 1, type E6+A2 (each dense open subset has the lower bound B(log B)^(rho−1), so the exceptional set is Zariski dense). The surfaces come from a classification of quasi-étale covers over C, not from a single explicit covering construction.

events.what_happened: Ulrich Derenthal, 'Manin's conjecture for the chordal cubic fourfold' (arXiv 2504.16051, v1 22 Apr 2025; 21 pages; the only version listed; no journal reference). The full text I read (first 100,000 of about 120,000 characters) proves the thin-set version over Q for the chordal (determinantal) cubic fourfold X in P^5 (the secant variety of the Veronese surface), via the symmetric square of P^2 and Schmidt's count of quadratic points. Theorem 1.1 gives asymptotics c B log B with error O(B) on three pieces X0, X+, X− that partition X(Q). Theorem 1.2 works on the smooth blow-up X~ = Hilb^2(P^2) over Q: after removing the thin set X~0 = h^{-1}(X0), the count is (c+ + c−) B log B, which the paper states is Peyre's constant. The acknowledgements thank E. Peyre and P. Salberger for discussions.
events.delivers: Thin-set form of the Manin asymptotic over Q for the chordal cubic fourfold: on the smooth blow-up, with a thin set removed, the count is (c+ + c−) B log B, stated to be Peyre's constant. On the singular cubic itself, asymptotics on three pieces. Restricted to Q and this one variety.

events.what_happened: Abdulmuhsin Alfaraj, 'Manin's Conjecture for Equivariant compactifications of forms of G_a^n' (arXiv 2505.04562, v1 7 May 2025; one version; no journal reference). Theorem 1.8 shows the leading constant equals alpha*(X) tau_X(X(A_F)), which the paper states agrees with Peyre's prediction. It also proves the Hasse principle and weak approximation for commutative unipotent groups, and works out P^(p−1).

events.delivers: Function-field (F_q(t), q large) all-heights asymptotic for split quintic del Pezzo surfaces; for lower-degree surfaces over F_q, lower bounds only. Number fields are not addressed.
events.remains: Number fields; the lower-degree asymptotics; small q.
events.direction: Analogue (function field): in favour, for F_q(t) and large q.

events.what_happened: Boaz Moerman, 'Manin's conjecture for M-points' (arXiv 2512.07654, v1 8 Dec 2025; v2 11 Dec 2025; v3 23 Feb 2026; 47 pages; a thesis-based paper, acknowledging Marta Pieropan). The full text proposes an asymptotic formula, Conjecture 1.4, for the number of M-points of bounded height on rationally connected varieties, extending Manin's conjecture and its Campana-point generalisation. M-points are special subsets of rational points defined by prescribed valuation conditions. The paper does not prove the general conjecture. It proves Theorem 1.7 (Fujita and b-invariants for Campana, Darmon and weak Campana points, no asymptotic). Theorem 1.12 proves the conjecture for split toric pairs over Q, attributed to a separate work.
events.delivers: A conjecture for M-points (subsets of rational points) on rationally connected varieties, with a leading constant identified only under extra hypotheses. Proved for split toric pairs over Q in a separate work. Not a settlement of the bullet.
events.remains: The general conjecture; M-points for non-toric varieties; whether M-points are within the bullet's 'certain subsets' is a reading question (see summary).
events.direction: A conjecture; generalises the counting statement to subsets of rational points. Not a resolution of any case of the bullet.

events.what_happened: Boaz Moerman, 'M-points of bounded height on toric varieties' (arXiv 2512.16746, v1 18 Dec 2025; v2 23 Feb 2026; 42 pages). The full text (first 100,000 of about 170,000 characters) proves an asymptotic count of M-points of bounded height on smooth proper split toric varieties over Q, for the height from any big and nef divisor class; Campana and weak Campana points are special cases, and the paper derives an asymptotic for rational points in the image of a toric rational map. The paper states that its result 'improves on the original proof of Manin's conjecture for toric varieties by Batyrev and Tschinkel', by controlling the error term.
events.revisions: v2 23 Feb 2026 (adds Corollary 1.6 and connections to the Loughran–Smeets conjecture, per the v2 comment on the abstract page).
events.delivers: Asymptotics for M-points on split toric varieties over Q, with a power-saving error term. A claimed improved error term for rational points on toric varieties, a case already settled by Batyrev–Tschinkel (1995). Does not touch the non-toric Fano case.
events.remains: M-points on non-toric varieties; the general conjecture; all non-toric Fano varieties.
events.direction: In favour, for the toric M-point case; it does not change the status of any non-toric case.

It proves no new number-field counting result.

events.what_happened: Dimitri Kanevsky, Julian Salazar and Matt Harvey, 'R-equivalence on Cubic Surfaces I: Existing Cases with Non-Trivial Universal Equivalence' (arXiv 2603.19215, v1 19 Mar 2026; 23 pages). The paper concerns R-equivalence on smooth cubic surfaces over p-adic fields with good reduction. It proves that for 2-adic surfaces with all-Eckardt reduction, R-equivalence is trivial or of exponent 2, and confirms that the diagonal cubic X^3 + Y^3 + Z^3 + zeta_3 T^3 = 0 over Q_2(zeta_3) has trivial R-equivalence, which the abstract says answers a question of Manin's from his 1972 book Cubic Forms. The paper does not count rational points of bounded height and does not concern the Manin conjecture as the bullet states it. The authors describe the paper as the first in a series from a year of work with generative AI models. The AI quotes below come from the arXiv HTML, read through a summarising fetch tool; verify them verbatim.
events.delivers: R-equivalence results (triviality for certain p-adic cubic surfaces, including the diagonal cubic over Q_2(zeta_3)). A different question: no counting of rational points of bounded height. Listed because its title and abstract name Manin and rational points on a Fano variety, and because it is an AI-involved result on rational points of cubic surfaces.
events.remains: Everything in the bullet's counting statement.
events.directly_checkable: The diagonal cubic over Q_2(zeta_3) is given by an explicit equation; the R-equivalence claim rests on the paper's argument, which I did not check.
events.doubts: The authors' AI disclosure says 'Our explorations began in March 2025, and so many of our interactions predate suggested norms on cataloguing and presenting AI use', and the paper states that a companion report is in preparation. Both are as the authors state them; I did not check the companion report.
events.direction: Different question (R-equivalence on p-adic cubic surfaces), so it neither moves nor settles the counting statement.

It states no new theorem; its main applications are over finite fields, with F_q(t) as the motivating case, and the Cohen–Jones–Segal discussion is over C.

events.what_happened: Qile Chen, Brian Lehmann and Sho Tanimoto, 'Manin's conjecture for semi-integral curves and A^1-connectedness' (arXiv 2605.19898, v1 19 May 2026; 47 pages). The full text I read (first 100,000 of about 163,000 characters) proves log Manin's conjecture for Campana rational curves and for A^1-curves on split toric varieties, for integral points, over F_q(t) per the text (Theorem 1.6; Theorem 1.8), combining the Cox-ring description of the moduli of rational curves with Batyrev-style counting. It presents these as a geometric explanation of the leading constant for Campana points proposed by Chow, Loughran, Takloo-Bighash and Tanimoto. It proves no number-field or Fano statement of the bullet's kind.
events.delivers: Log and integral-point analogues for split toric varieties over F_q(t): Campana rational curves and A^1-curves. A different question from counting rational points of bounded height on Fano varieties over number fields.
events.remains: Number fields; Fano varieties; rational rather than integral points.
events.direction: Different question (log/integral points, function field): neither moves nor settles the bullet.

events.what_happened: Christian Bernert, Ulrich Derenthal and Florian Wilsch, 'Equidistribution and the torsor method' (arXiv 2607.14866, v1 16 Jul 2026; 23 pages). The full text I read (first 100,000 of about 152,000 characters) proves equidistribution and Manin's conjecture for rational points outside the lines on smooth split quintic del Pezzo surfaces over number fields, for any anticanonical height. Proposition 3.1 gives the asymptotic N(H,B) ~ alpha(X) tau_H(X(A_K)) divided by a congruence factor, times B (log B)^4, with alpha(X) = 1/144: the constant has Peyre's form. The paper does not explicitly verify that the Brauer–Manin set is all of X(A_K) for this surface.
events.delivers: For smooth split quintic del Pezzo surfaces over number fields: the Manin asymptotic (with Peyre-form constant) and equidistribution on U(K), the complement of the lines, for any anticanonical height. One class of surfaces; the lines are excluded from the count.
events.remains: Non-split quintic surfaces; singular quintic surfaces; the points on the lines; del Pezzo surfaces of other degrees.
events.doubts: The Brauer–Manin set's equality with X(A_K) is not verified in the text I read; the constant's identification with Peyre's is by form (Proposition 3.1), not by a separate calculation in the part I read.
events.direction: In favour: the Zariski-open count (complement of the lines) is shown to have the expected asymptotic for these surfaces over number fields.

events.what_happened: Sho Tanimoto, 'On Manin's conjecture for quartic del Pezzo fibrations' (arXiv 2608.28471, v1 28 Aug 2026; 76 pages). The full text I read (first 100,000 of about 155,000 characters) extends the homological sieve to certain quartic del Pezzo fibrations over curves B over F_q, with fibres of Picard rank 2 that have two birational morphisms to non-split quadric surfaces. It proves a version of Manin's conjecture for these, including an all-heights limit for blow-up models (Theorem 1.4), using the positive-characteristic 3-dimensional MMP and a space-of-sections argument. The acknowledgements and funding are visible in the text. AI: the author writes 'ChatGPT was used to proofread this paper and to revise the introduction'. That use is proofreading and copy-editing, not load-bearing mathematics, so it is not listed under ai.systems.

events.remains: Number fields; general quartic fibrations; the quintic analogue (sketched only, Remark 1.5 as read).
events.direction: Analogue (function field): in favour, for F_q(B) and these fibrations.

summary: Found and read: 30 events, of which 10 predate the frozen revision (Batyrev–Tschinkel 1995 for toric varieties; Frei–Pieropan 2013 for one singular quartic del Pezzo; Lehmann–Tanimoto 2016 on thin exceptional sets; Gorodnik–Maucourant–Oh 2008 from a snippet only; the LST thin-set verification, 2018 per an unopened snippet and not located on arXiv; Blomer–Brüdern–Derenthal–Gagliardi 2022 for type N spherical Fano threefolds; Bonolis–Browning–Huang 2022 for bidegree (1,2) threefolds; Gao 2022 for the dimension-2 counterexample to the closed-set form; Wang 2023 for the ax+b group over Q; Gao 2023 for the Batyrev–Tschinkel five-fold, in which the closed-set form is shown to fail and the LST set identified with a thin set). The in-window events, on the number-field statement for specific varieties: Bernert–Derenthal (May 2024) gives the full Manin asymptotic with Peyre's constant for split smooth quintic del Pezzo surfaces over any number field, counting the complement of the lines; Pieropan–Schindler (March 2024) gives asymptotics on open pieces of subvarieties of toric varieties over Q, but the paper says only 'compatible with' the conjecture and does not identify the constant with Peyre's; Gao (June 2024) gives counterexamples to the closed-set form for four singular Du Val del Pezzo surfaces of degrees 1–3, and none in degree 4 or more; Derenthal (April 2025) gives the thin-set form over Q for the chordal cubic fourfold, with the constant stated to be Peyre's; Bernert–Derenthal–Wilsch (July 2026) gives the asymptotic with equidistribution for split smooth quintic del Pezzo surfaces over number fields, counting outside the lines, for any anticanonical height. Function-field analogues (Alfaraj 2025; Das–Lehmann–Tanimoto–Tosteson 2025; Tanimoto 2025 and 2026; Bernert–Faisant–Glas 2026), geometric Manin results (Hase-Liu 2024 and 2025; Jovinelly–Okamura 2024), log and integral-point results (Chen–Lehmann–Tanimoto 2026), M-points (Moerman, one conjecture and one toric theorem), a survey (Lehmann–Tanimoto 2026), and a non-counting R-equivalence result (Kanevsky et al.) are recorded as neighbouring events, each with its scope note. Close calls: (a) Gao's Zariski-dense exceptional sets defeat the closed-set reading, but I did not verify whether they are thin, so they may be consistent with the thin-set reading the modern literature uses; (b) the Derenthal, Bernert–Derenthal and Bernert–Derenthal–Wilsch results are full resolutions for their varieties under the thin-set or open-set reading, so their status depends on which reading the bullet's 'certain subsets' carries; (c) Pieropan–Schindler counts on open subsets of subvarieties rather than of the Fano variety itself, and its constant is not identified with Peyre's. Wikipedia's article (last edited 30 March 2026) says the conjecture 'has been proved for special families of varieties' and 'is still open in general', which matches what I found. AI: no AI system is credited with a counting result for this bullet. Three in-window papers name AI: Kanevsky et al. (Gemini models, load-bearing lemma proofs, but for R-equivalence); Alexeev–Schreieder (GPT-6 Astra and GPT, load-bearing ideas, but for the existence of rational points on cubic surfaces); and Tanimoto 2608.28471 (ChatGPT for proofreading and revising the introduction only, not listed as a system). All other sources read to the first 100,000 characters named no AI system. Magma (computer algebra, not AI) appears in Gao 2024 and Gao 2022. The three AI quotes from the Kanevsky and Alexeev–Schreieder papers came from a summarising fetch and need checking verbatim against the PDF. I did not find a Lean formalisation of any counting result for this bullet.
competing_reading: Read 'in certain subsets' as the thin-set (Peyre) formulation, the modern standard. Under that reading Gao's Zariski-dense exceptional sets are not counterexamples if they are thin, which I did not verify, and the in-window results of Bernert–Derenthal (2024), Derenthal (2025) and Bernert–Derenthal–Wilsch (2026) are real partial resolutions for their varieties. Read it instead as Manin's original open-subset (Zariski-closed removal) form. Then Gao's 2022 and 2024 papers show that form fails for specific singular del Pezzo surfaces, Gao's 2023 paper shows it fails for the Batyrev–Tschinkel five-fold, and Derenthal's 2025 result, which removes a thin set, does not settle the open-subset statement. A third reading restricts the bullet to rational points on the variety itself, which would exclude the Pieropan–Schindler subvariety counts and the M-point results; a fourth would include the M-point conjecture of Moerman (2025) as a generalisation of the bullet.
what_would_settle_it: (a) Whether the exceptional sets in Gao 2024 (arXiv 2406.16240, Theorem 1.2 and the thin-set section) and Gao 2022 (arXiv 2207.04348) are thin, i.e. contained in a thin set in the sense of Serre, which would be checked against the LST thin-set theorem; (b) the full text of Derenthal 2025 (arXiv 2504.16051) and Bernert–Derenthal–Wilsch 2026 (arXiv 2607.14866), in particular the Section 5 constant calculation and the Brauer–Manin set; (c) whether Pieropan–Schindler's constant equals Peyre's constant; (d) the verbatim AI sentences in arXiv 2603.19215 and arXiv 2609.15930; (e) the unread tails of the long HTML papers, for acknowledgement and AI statements; and (f) a decision on which reading of 'certain subsets' the counting pass will apply.

event.what_happened: Pieropan and Schindler, 'Points of bounded height on certain subvarieties of toric varieties' (arXiv 2403.19397, v1 28 Mar 2024; v2 7 Oct 2024, minor revision; Algebra & Number Theory 19 (2025), 2281–2306, DOI 10.2140/ant.2025.19.2281). The full text (first 100,000 characters of about 130,000) combines the split torsor method and the hyperbola method. For subvarieties V of smooth split proper toric varieties over Q it counts Q-rational points (and Campana points) of bounded height: Theorem 1.1 (linear complete intersections, L ample, counted on V ∩ T, asymptotic c B (log B)^(b−1)); Theorem 1.2 (bihomogeneous complete intersections, counted on V ∩ W ∩ T with an explicitly removed open set W); Theorem 1.3 (Campana points on diagonal complete intersections). The leading constant is given by a formula the paper does not identify with Peyre's constant; the paper says the results are 'compatible with' Manin's conjecture, since L restricted to V is −K_V by adjunction.
event.delivers: Asymptotic counts with the expected (log B) exponent for rational points on open pieces (V ∩ T, or V ∩ W ∩ T) of certain subvarieties of split smooth proper toric varieties over Q: linear complete intersections, bihomogeneous complete intersections, and Campana points on diagonal complete intersections. The leading constant is not identified with Peyre's constant.
event.remains: Identification of the leading constant with Peyre's constant; Fano varieties outside these families; non-split and non-toric ambient cases; the removed open sets are not exceptional sets in the thin-set sense.
